verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “I have this like really crazy headache that's been going on for a few days… around three days ago, maybe,” matching a ‘crazy’ headache for about 3 days.

Location: “it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly, um, around my right eye.” Course: “it kind of comes and goes… it is there all the time, but like sometimes it's stronger.” Severity: when asked 1–10, patient answers “Ohh it's probably a eight.” This supports diffuse headache worst around right eye, constant with intermittent flares, max 8/10.

Onset: “it developed gradually, I guess.” Worsening: doctor asks, “you think the headache is getting worse over the last three days?” and patient answers “Yeah.” This supports gradual onset and daily worsening.

Patient reports, “I got this like weird shooting lights. And like now like light is quite annoying, my eyes… it hurts to look… at bright lights.” This supports initial photopsia (“shooting lights”) and photophobia.

Nausea: Doctor asks, “Any nausea or any vomiting?” Patient: “well I'm like basically, I I'm sick with the headache. But I, no vomiting.” This implies nausea without vomiting. Difficulty focusing at work: “it's hard to focus though. So, I I had to take a couple of days off work, actually,” and later “I work in IT… it kind of is difficult to focus.”

Vision: “Any loss of vision or blurry vision?” Patient: “Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say.” Neck: “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?” Patient: “No.” Neuro: “Any difficulty with speaking…?” “No.” “Any… weakness in your arms and legs?” “No.” Systemic: “Any temperatures, or fevers?” “No.” “Any rashes at all, on your skin?” “no not that I've noticed.” Trauma: “any recent head injuries at all?” “no.” This supports all listed denials.

Ibuprofen: “I tried uh Ibuprofen… I took, like a few. Um for the last two days, basically… But it doesn't really help, no.” Dose clarified later: “How many tablets did you take of Ibuprofen?” Patient: “Uh, three a day.” Regular meds: When asked “do you take any regular medication?” Patient: “Uh, no no.”
When asked, “do you have any other medical history?” patient replies, “Yeah, I think so. It's just the headache,” indicating no other past medical history volunteered.
Family history: “Any history of migraines at all?” Patient: “Not myself… But my sister and my mom have them quite frequently.”

Work: “I work in IT. So I work with computers a lot. So it kind of is difficult to focus.” Living situation: “I live with housemates. So, three of them. So we're four.” This supports heavy screen-use IT job and three housemates.
Glasses: “Do you wear glasses?” Patient: “Yes, I do.” Duration: “I've been wearing them since I was five , five year old.”
Social history: “I socially smoke. And I drink only socially.”
Stress: When asked about stress/anxiety, patient says, “Well, it's been a bit stressful, kicking off a new project. But um, yeah nothing out of the ordinary, really.” This supports mild work stress.
Allergies: “Do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “Mm not that I know of.” This supports no known drug allergies.

Doctor’s assessment: “I… unfortunately I do think this could be, a headache very similar to a migraine… the history is very suggestive of it, given your mum and your sister also migraines.” Red flags specifically denied: no vision loss, speech difficulty, limb weakness, neck stiffness, fever, rash, or recent head injury. This supports migraine-like acute severe headache with family predisposition and no red-flag features on history.

NSAID use: Patient: “I tried uh Ibuprofen… for the last two days… But it doesn't really help, no.” Doctor: “my only worry is, I'm not sure whether you're taking, the correct dose. You can take up to two tablets, three times a day. So… there's definitely room for, improvement there.” This supports that NSAID use has been ineffective and suboptimal.

Social tobacco: “I socially smoke.” Eye exam: Doctor says, “have you had any recent eye check…?” Patient: “No… it's quite a long time.” Doctor: “I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.” This supports social smoking and being due/overdue for eye exam.
Doctor explicitly counsels: “You can take up to two tablets, three times a day,” referring to Ibuprofen dosing, which is counseling on max 2 tablets three times daily.

Doctor: “I can prescribe you something stronger, like Naproxen… We can also add in other, painkillers like, Paracetamol, or Codeine. Which might be helpful as well.” This matches offering Naproxen and possibly adding Paracetamol or Codeine.
Plan: “It may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's, you know, if there's any triggers which could be causing your headaches to become worse.”

Eye exam recommendation: “if you feel that you are, your eyes are straining. Um I would always recommend having a repeat eye test done.” This matches recommending an eye exam if visual strain persists.

Follow-up: “I'd like you to come back and see me, in about uh, a week's time, week to two weeks' time.” Safety net: “if your headaches aren't getting any better, or they're getting worse… give me a call, or come back and see me sooner… if you're having any problems with your vision, or weakness in your arms and legs… just give me a call, and come back and see me.” This supports follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner with vision changes, focal deficits, or worsening headache.
